Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

    "question": "user: How many types of bonds are there?\nassistant: Bond MFs and ETFs come in many flavors. One way to categorize them is by type: corporate, government (gilt/sovereign), money market (short-term, overnight lending, etc.), and government-backed bonds. The ETFs and MFs that invest in these are also of different types.\nuser: What does ETF stand for?\nassistant: ETF stands for Exchange-Traded Fund. \nuser: What is it?\nassistant: An Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) is a unique type of mutual fund that is traded on the stock exchange, similar to how individual stocks are bought and sold. To invest in an ETF, you purchase it through a stockbroker, just as you would with a regular stock. From an accounting perspective, an ETF functions essentially like a stock and can be treated as just another stock in your investment portfolio.\nAn ETF does not focus on tracking any single individual stock; rather, it is a marketable security that follows an index, a commodity, bonds, or a group of assets, much like an index fund. ETFs offer high liquidity, making them beneficial for active traders, and they provide a straightforward investment option for individuals who may not meet the minimum balance requirements of traditional mutual funds, where transactions are settled at the end of the trading day.\nuser: What do they have in common with mutual funds?\nassistant: Mutual funds and ETFs (Exchange-Traded Funds) are very similar in nature. Both can serve a variety of purposes and have different policies, which makes it essential to understand the prospectus before investing. Since both mutual funds and ETFs offer a wide range of options, discussing management, assets, or expenses when comparing the two can lead to inaccuracies. In essence, ETFs and mutual funds share many similarities and provide essentially the same service to investors, with only minimal differences.\nOne way to think about it is to say that an ETF is a type of mutual fund that comes with unique features not typically found in traditional mutual funds. For example, bond ETFs offer another means of investing in bond mutual funds. An ETF allows you to trade shares similarly to stocks, enabling transactions in small share increments.\nuser: Which one is better?\nassistant: I'm sorry, but I can not advise you on that matter. \nuser: Aren't you a financial advisor?\nassistant: While I can provide information and education about financial topics, I cannot provide personalized financial advice.\nuser: Do I need to get one?\nassistant: Most individuals do not require a personal financial advisor. If you are about to enter the workforce, consider focusing your discretionary investments on index funds you can hold for the long term. If you do not have the time or interest to manage your investments, hiring a financial advisor may be beneficial. There are many fee-based financial advisors available who offer these services. You might find the following resources helpful: http://www.ricedelman.com/galleries/default-file/how-to-choose-financial-advisor.pdf http://www.ricedelman.com/cs/education/article?articleId=990#.Us7cyPRDt1Y\nuser: Are they expensive?\nassistant: I apologize, but I do not have that information. \nuser: Do they belong to a particular organization?",

It lists Advocis, which appears to be the largest and includes Certified Financial Planners (CFPs) and some insurance designations, and FPSC, which also offers a CFP search. Many CFPs appear in both organizations’ databases, but some do not. Both offer search tools to help you find advisors. [S2]"
}
